verdict.tagline: Deep strategy awaits, though technical quirks and steep curves test patience.
for_you_if: you love intricate turn based strategy
you can master complex empire systems
you enjoy losing hours to sprawling campaigns

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a paywall locking certain civilizations behind additional purchases.

citations.review_text: I tried, I really tried to like it. I was put off by the Pay Wall on most Civs, but thought, hey if the core is good its maybe worth it. But while the graphics are lovely, the mechanics are clunky, the research tree is disjoined and lacking intuitive direction that earlier titles gave. Honestly I just finished a game of Civ 4 and it was better in every way then Civ6, I have no intention of even trying Civ 7. The devs have destroyed this franchise and the original developers of Test of Time should be rolling in their grave with the way the company has advanced Civilisation titles by gradually eroding everything fun about them.

Changing skin color of historical figures from cultures is outrageous and unacceptable art design choice. On top of this forcing players to pay for the countries they would want to play with is LOW. You are strategy game about civilizations at least get something right... I am really upset and disappointed that i have purchased this game.
you have to pay for characters :(

claims.claim: Reviewers find the game highly addictive, causing them to lose track of time while playing.

citations.review_text: Fun but highly addictive, your day will disappear before you even know it!!
It takes me about 10 hours to learn Civilization VI, but once you get the hang of it it’s addicting. Even when you don't really need or intend to play you just end up playing anyway.

Amazing, probably a bit too addictive. You have to set a time limit and immediately stop otherwise you will keep on playing for another hour. But other than that i would highly reccomend this for anyone who like strategy.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention needing to consult external guides or videos to learn the new district mechanics and game changes.

citations.review_text:
This is a strange one for this franchise. Since always Civ allowed you to play simply, and introduced new mechanics over time with advancing technology. This makes the game easy to get into and learn as you play, while retaining the complexity needed for an engaging 4X game. Civ 6 commits a cardinal sin: districts. A district is a concept taken from the future and contrivingly enforced upon the past. Before you make a choice of which district to build where, you're going to need to stop playing and go online and read in great detail about districts. Contrivances are a huge game-killer for me, and I could never get over this one.

I regard Civ 4 as the apex of the series, being the last of the original line of games (square map plus military unit stacking), and the first of the beautiful ones. But in a way, Civ 6 might be a beginning of a whole new line of Civ games, wherein you can't just play and learn as you go, but have to start by obtaining encyclopedic knowledge of a contrived game mechanic.
Enjoyed Civ V, it is quite the difference so getting up to date took some time and videos. The game is great thought!

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the learning curve as difficult or overwhelming at the start, requiring time to figure out the systems.

citations.review_text: At the start, I hated this game with a passion, cause the amount of information the game gives you at the start overwhelmed me. Even with the tutorial felt like it wasn't helping. So, the first 3 games, i kept loosing by a big margin. Suddenly, it click, now i can't stop playing. I've now done 2 all nighters in a row.

there is no other game like Sid Meier's Civ 6, Civ 7 kinda sucks as of now, so i'm playing this amazing game while waiting for them to fix Civ 7. it was very complicated to learn this game, but once i got the hang of it, i started liking it more and more. tbh the early and mid game are the most fun, the late game lacks in a lot of areas, because unless you are in an active war, you are just waiting for your stuff to finish building. that's kinda it for the late game in terms of gameplay. but nonetheless, Civ 6 is still very fun, and i haven't even tried other kinds of map generation or challenges. wait for a big sale to get the game and all the DLCs for cheap, it's worth it. especially if you play it with friends
honestly this game makes me want to blow myself up but its a fun experience especially if you're open to the required time sink to become acclimated to the gameplay loop

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that DLC content is advertised or pushed heavily within the game interface.

citations.review_text:
At first I thought this game was much worse than Civ V, but honestly I quite like it, still maybe not as good as Civ V but definitely a great game either way.

The Civ VII advertisements are annoying but you can get a mod which removes them from the home page so it isn't really an issue.

Just play Civ 5 instead. The only reason I play this one is because my friends refuse to just go back to peak. I'm tired of DLC being shoved down my throat and shown when I don't have the content too. Not that the other one didn't have DLC, but it just feels even more forceful here with required online just like others said.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that loading saved multiplayer games can result in bugs that break the complete multiplayer save.

citations.review_text:
The computer-controlled civs are passive and mostly unchallenging once you get the hang of things, even on higher difficulties. Ending a match can be a bit of a slog also. Multiplayer with friends is how I play and that's good fun. I like the changes and additions from Civ V.

Game versions are different between operating systems, which can be a hassle to sort out. "Play by cloud" is at times unreliable.

Its a good game overall, but i f*king hate it, that the developers cannot fix that damn multiplayer bug when loading in a saved multiplayer game and nobody can do ♥♥♥♥. The complete MP-save is broken now. The bug already existed in Civ 5 and now in Civ 6 as well. But instead of fixing old bugs they instead push out a new f*king Civ game with the same bug again. Never buying another Civ until this ♥♥♥♥ is fixed for good.

claims.claim: Reviewers note problems with online services and account age verification preventing multiplayer access.

citations.review_text: Terrible, also you can't play offline LAN due to stupid "age verification" non-sense so....screw 2K games, will never purchase another one of their games again.

The game's online services seem broken.

Randomly I have an error that says my 2k account is too young to play online. I never made a 2k account before. I made a 2k account and linked it with an appropriate age, and it still does not work.

And after reading online other people have found or not found solutions, the solutions I tried did not work. So I cannot recommend this game with it literally being broken.
